verdict.rationale: Aider documents its own programmatic interfaces: a Python scripting API (`Coder.create(...)` then `coder.run(...)` to execute an instruction and return) and a non-interactive `--message` CLI mode that applies edits and exits. That lets an agent or script drive the product directly. However, there is no network or REST API, and probes for an OpenAPI spec all returned 404, so the API is a thin, single-page, in-process Python interface rather than a fully specified public API. Missing for 10: a full API reference with method and parameter docs, an HTTP/REST or OpenAPI-described endpoint, stability/versioning guarantees for the Python API, and independent hands-on corroboration of programmatic use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: Aider takes a `--message` argument, where you can give it a natural language instruction. It will do that one thing, apply the edits to the files and then exit.
